tips: Press the up arrow (or the middle mouse button) to take out your phone.
Payphones still work: stand in front of one and press F to pick up the receiver.
Your phone has no Wi-Fi bill but a data allowance. Big downloads are cheaper over a café's network.
A cold GPS takes a while to find the satellites. Open sky helps; deep canyons of towers do not.
Your notebook needs somewhere to sit or lean. Press N near a bench, a table or a counter.
Every building has an inside. Walk through a door and take the lift by clicking its buttons.
Brick buildings often have fire escapes. Walk along the outer edge of a landing to climb.
The night is quieter: fewer witnesses, emptier streets, shorter shifts.
Citizens post on Streetwire about what they see. Read it to learn what happened across town.
The news on your phone comes from things that really happened in the city.
When the power goes out, traffic lights stop and every crossing becomes a four-way stop.
Stay away from the fire zone beyond the fence. The ground there is hot, and the air is worse.
Each citizen has a home, a job and a routine. Follow someone and you will learn their day.
Calls cost credit. Dial *100# to check your balance and top up.
Press F3 to hide the debug lines and take a clean screenshot.
Press R to change how many rows the world is drawn with, and V for how sharp the glyphs look.
Open your notebook with N, then use iwconfig to see whether its card has joined any network.
A cafe's open Wi-Fi is the easy way in. Join it with iwconfig, then run dhclient for an address.
Once you have an address, mmap lists the machines on the network and the services they answer on.
Most systems hide behind a weak password. Point bruter at a host's console and let it work the list.
The GRIDLINK networks by the substations are the utility's own, still on old WEP that gives up its key.
Technicians log in over GRIDLINK in the clear. Leave tdump listening and it catches what they type.
Open a console on a host with tnet, or talk straight to a substation's breaker over mbus.
Everything you touch leaves a trail: the network logs your notebook right where it stands.
